definition: To keep asking someone for something so often that it becomes annoying.
example: The young writer importuned the editor with weekly letters until she agreed to read his manuscript.
nuance: To beseech stresses how strongly you feel when you ask, while to importune stresses asking so persistently that you become a nuisance.
prompt: A young boy keeps asking his parents for a puppy at every meal.
options: Night after night, the boy would importune his parents for a puppy.
The boy waited for an importune moment, when his parents seemed relaxed, to bring up puppies.
To importune his parents, the boy promised himself he would never mention puppies again.
His father would importune him by agreeing to the puppy the first time it came up.
reasons: Raising the same request at every dinner is exactly the kind of tiresome pressing the verb describes.
This mixes up the verb with the adjective "opportune," which means well-timed.
Deciding never to ask again is the reverse of pestering someone with requests.
Granting a wish right away is not making repeated demands, so the verb has nothing to do here.

A single word of thanks is neither a request nor persistent, so it cannot be pestering.
Chasing strangers with the same plea over and over is persistent, unwelcome asking.
